response: Physicians who opt to treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) in postmenopausal women empirically should consider prescribing drugs other than fluoroquinolones. This is due to concerns about resistance rates and the need for concomitant longitudinal surveillance of both antibiotic utilization patterns and uropathogen resistance rates. It is recommended that healthcare providers consider alternative treatment options and monitor the effectiveness of these treatments in order to provide the best possible care for older women with UTIs in Israel.
